chunks: And from him (Al-Husayn ibn Idris) from Al-Hasan ibn al-Hawla from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Kurdawayh al-Hamdani who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about making up the Witr prayer, so he said: 'Whatever is after midday is even (double), two by two.'

So it is possible that the meaning of these hadiths is for one who wishes to make it up while sitting, despite his ability to stand, because in this state he should pray two rak'ahs in place of each single rak'ah, which clarifies what we mentioned.
ai.seo_question: How is the Witr prayer performed if made up after midday or while sitting?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes that Witr, when performed after midday (Zawal), is treated as an even prayer (Shaf') consisting of pairs of two rak'ahs. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence for those performing Qada (make-up) while seated despite having the ability to stand, where the principle dictates praying two rak'ahs for every single missed rak'ah to ensure completeness.
